### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, five activities — A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — each ran in about 16–23 in 100 traces (31–46 of 200 each) and never shared a trace; their shares sum to about 100 in 100, so essentially every trace contained exactly one of them. In the later window they are nearly gone: A20 and A21 appear in 0 of 200 traces, the other three in 1 of 200. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012]
- Earlier, each of the five co-occurred with A24, A25 and A26 in every trace where it appeared (these three anchors ran in all 200 traces in both windows); in the later window such co-occurrence survives in at most about 1 in 200 traces. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL013, REL014, REL015]
- Earlier, the alternative step sat in one of two slots: in about 39 in 100 traces the sequence was A24 → (one of the five) → A25 → A26, and in about 61 in 100 it was A24 → A25 → (one of the five) → A26. Accordingly, A24's outgoing transitions went to A25 in about 61 in 100 cases and to one of the five otherwise, A25's went to A26 in about 39 in 100 cases and to one of the five otherwise, and A26 always came exactly 3 steps after A24. [DIR005, DIR006, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, REL005, REL010, REL014]
- In the later window only the direct shape remains: A24's transitions go to A25 in about 98–99 in 100 cases, A25's transitions go to A26 in essentially all cases, and A26 comes 2 steps after A24 in about 98–99 in 100 traces. [DIR005, DIR006, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]
- Individual alternatives had occupied both slots earlier (for example, A15 preceded A25 in about 10 in 100 traces and followed it in about 13–14 in 100, and was followed by A26 in about 59 in 100 of its runs); the after-window profiles of these edges rest on a single trace each. [REL005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]
- A26 remained in every trace and its mean relative position moved slightly earlier (about 0.56 to 0.55), consistent with one middle event dropping out of traces; the position figures for the five activities afterwards rest on at most one trace. [POS005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative step formed by A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 is no longer executed: earlier, every trace inserted exactly one of these five mutually exclusive activities either between A24 and A25 (about 39 in 100 traces) or between A25 and A26 (about 61 in 100), whereas in the later window traces proceed directly from A24 through A25 to A26 and each of the five appears in at most 1 of 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR005, DIR006, LAG006, REL004, REL006, REL011, REL015]

The change is shown directly and consistently: participation collapses from 31–46 to 0–1 traces per activity, the successor profiles of A24 and A25 each collapse to a single successor, the A24→A26 distance shortens from 3 to 2 steps, and every pair relation between the five and the anchors flips from always co-occurring to never co-occurring. All 38 qualifying items belong to the control-flow family, against roughly 0.46 expected by chance, so the ensemble is many times what an unchanged process typically produces, and the items describe one coherent structural difference rather than scattered effects. [OCC003, DIR005, DIR006, LAG006, REL011, REL001]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish whether the five activities were removed from the process or are now always bypassed, since both produce the same observations, and zero participation only means they were not observed in this sample; the residual after-window routing profiles rest on single traces and may reflect a very small remaining participation rather than a new fixed order. [OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004]
